definition: Reasoning about the relationships among entities rather than their individual properties — a hallmark of structured cognition that relation networks and GNNs target.
details: Reasoning about the relationships among entities rather than their individual properties — a hallmark of structured cognition that relation networks and GNNs target.

explainer.lead: It reasons about relationships among entities rather than their individual properties. It is a hallmark of structured cognition, and it is what relation networks and graph neural networks target.

tiers.eli5: It works out how things connect — who is next to, above or linked to whom — instead of describing each thing alone.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers evaluate models on relational tasks such as ordering and comparison to check they capture structure. The pitfall is that models can fit surface features and fail when object order or counts shift.
tiers.paperLevel: Framed as computing outputs from pairwise or higher-order interactions among entity representations. Known limits: generalisation to unseen relation combinations and to larger sets than seen in training.

explainer.example: Given a set of objects with positions, a model must answer which object is furthest left, a task impossible from single-object features alone.
